title: x402 LLM Gateway — pay-per-request AI, settled on Stellar
description: Product pitch for x402 LLM Gateway: HTTP 402 stablecoin micropayments for LLM APIs on Stellar.

voice.style: Read the following product-demo narration as a confident technical founder: warm, clear and unhurried. Keep an even pace, put slight emphasis on product claims, and stay measured on risk and limitations. Do not oversell.

cues.text: Every AI product eventually hits the same wall: API keys, quotas, and invoices.
Access to a model is gated by billing, not by the model.
An account, an API key, a quota. An agent cannot open one.
Traffic is bursty, but the bill is flat for capacity you never use.
And every team rebuilds metering, invoicing and dunning.
The fix is already in the HTTP spec — unused since 1997.
402 Payment Required — a status code reserved for exactly this.
x402 makes it real: a quote, a payment, then a retry.
No signup, no subscription, no API key — just a wallet and a price.
Here is the whole money path. The gateway is a reverse proxy, OpenAI-compatible.
One: the caller sends a chat request. With no payment, the gateway answers 402 with a quote.
Two: the client pays the quoted amount in USDC on Stellar — typically in about five seconds.
Three: the gateway verifies the transaction against Horizon and the Soroban contracts, then atomically claims the hash.
Four: the request is forwarded upstream and the caller receives the model response plus a payment receipt.
This is not a mock-up — these are live responses from the gateway running against Stellar testnet.
An unpaid request returns a real quote: amount, asset, issuer, destination, and an expiry window.
The client pays one tenth of a USDC — a real, on-chain payment.
Retry with that hash: HTTP 200 and a payment receipt.
Pay once, spend once — replaying the hash is refused.
A forged hash is refused too. The gateway fails closed.
And the payment is public on Stellar Expert.
Providers get a real operational surface, not just a proxy.
Realtime revenue, paid versus unpaid traffic, and latency.
Routes carry their own upstream, model and pricing.
Every payment is recorded with its hash, payer and ledger.
Plus a full audit trail, webhooks, and escrow for prepaid credit.
Under the hood: a Nx monorepo with a NestJS gateway, a Next.js dashboard, and fifteen shared packages.
Replay protection is layered three deep — Redis for speed, Postgres as the authority, Soroban as permanent on-chain proof.
On-chain, the verifier contract stores each used hash as its own ledger entry, so gas stays flat as history grows.
And payments are bound to a quote window, which is what stops an old transaction being replayed for free access.
Why Stellar? Because the economics only work when settlement costs almost nothing.
Fees around one hundred-thousandth of a dollar, five-second finality, native USDC, and Soroban for verification.
That makes a tenth-of-a-cent payment viable — which is the whole point.
API keys require trust. Subscriptions require commitment. This requires neither.
This is engineered like infrastructure: lint, unit tests, an end-to-end suite, contract tests and a size gate.
Plus gitleaks, Trivy, OSV scanning and a ZAP baseline scan on every push.
The contracts are self-tested and live on testnet. An independent audit is the gate to mainnet.
x402 LLM Gateway. Pay per request. Settle on Stellar.
Clone it, run the quickstart, send your first unpaid request.
